transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can I ask your name and what brings you in to see me today?

I'm Mark. Um... well, I guess I'm here because... most nights, after my wife goes to sleep, I, uh... I end up in the kitchen. And I just... I eat a lot. Like, way more than a normal amount. If there's leftover fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls... I just keep eating until, you know, a whole tray or half the fridge is just gone.
When you're in the kitchen eating all of that food, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah... I suppose. It's just... once I take that first bite, it kind of feels like the decision is already made for me. I'll be standing there, telling myself, you know, "Mark, stop now." But... my hands just keep fixing another plate. Or opening another container. I just... yeah. I don't stop.
Does this eating behavior cause you a lot of distress, or does it interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah... I guess it does. I, uh... I don't really do as much as I used to. I used to help out a lot with these community planning meetings, setting up local events... but I've kind of pulled back from all of that lately. 

I just feel... drained. And, I don't know, embarrassed, maybe. I'm just afraid people are going to look at me and realize I'm not really holding things together the way I used to. So it's just easier to stay away.
When you're eating in the kitchen like that, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual, or feeling uncomfortably full by the end?

Yeah... I suppose I do. Um... I eat really fast during those times. So fast I barely even taste it... which, I don't know, I used to take pride in cooking that food. But... yeah. Sometimes I'm just standing there at the counter and... I'm swallowing big bites before I've even finished chewing the last one. So... yeah.
Do you usually eat alone during these times because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?
I... I don't really know. I guess I'm usually alone when it happens, but... I haven't really thought about it like that. I'm just by myself a lot of the time anyway.
Do these episodes of eating a lot usually happen specifically at night, after you've already had dinner and maybe even after you've gone to bed for a while?

Yeah... um, usually later on. I mean, a lot of the time I'm not even hungry at all. I might have just finished eating dinner with my wife... but then later I still go back in there. I just... start picking at the leftovers, and then... I don't know, it just turns into another full-on spread. So... yeah.
After these episodes of eating, do you find yourself feeling guilty, ashamed, or disgusted with yourself?

Yeah. I mean... yeah. I feel pretty sick with myself afterward. It's just... I don't know, people think I'm this organized, strong guy, and then... I'm just sitting there. Feeling ashamed. Guilty. Disgusted that I... let it happen again.
When you're eating all that food in the kitchen, do you feel like you're not fully in control of yourself, like you're unable to stop eating even though you want to?

I guess... yeah. It's like... once I take that first bite, the decision's already made. I'll be standing there, telling myself... you know, 'George, stop now.' But my hands just... they keep fixing another plate. Opening another container. I just... I can't seem to stop it.
When you're eating all that food in the kitchen, do you feel like you're not fully in control of yourself, like you're unable to stop eating even though you want to?
Yeah... um, like I just said. It's... I can't stop. I don't really know what else to tell you about it.
When you're eating all that food in the kitchen, do you feel a loss of control, like you can't stop eating even though you want to?
I... look, we just went over this. It's the same thing. Once I start, I can't stop. I'm just... I'm out of control. I don't know why you keep asking me the same question.
Has this eating behavior affected your relationships, work, or other important areas of your life?

I suppose... yeah. I don't really do as much as I used to. I've stopped going to the community planning meetings, and... helping out with events. I just kind of pulled back from all that. 

I'm just too drained most of the time. And... I don't know, I guess I'm just afraid people are going to notice that I'm not really holding things together the way I used to. It's... it's embarrassing. So I just stay away.
Have these nighttime eating episodes caused problems in your relationships, work, or other important areas of your life?
I... didn't I just answer this? Like I just said, I stopped going to the community stuff. I just stay away from people. I don't really have anything else to say about it.
How often do these nighttime eating episodes happen—do they occur at least once a week, and have they been happening for several months?

I guess... yeah, it's been happening for a while. For months now. I... I can't really think of a single week where it didn't happen at least once. Usually... usually it's several nights a week. Just... after my wife goes to bed.
When you're having these nighttime eating episodes, do you usually feel down, depressed, or hopeless at those times?
I don't... no. I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel depressed or hopeless when it's happening. I'm just... eating. That's all.
Do you feel that these nighttime eating episodes are affecting your sense of self-worth or causing you emotional pain beyond what you've already described?

I just... it's hard to talk about. I guess it does affect me. Afterward, I just... I feel sick with myself. Everyone thinks I'm this organized, strong guy, and then... I'm just sitting there in the kitchen. Ashamed. Just disgusted that I let it happen again. I feel so guilty about it.

Do you feel that your nighttime eating episodes are causing you significant distress or problems in areas of your life beyond what you've already mentioned, such as socially, at work, or in your family life?

I guess... yeah, it has. I used to be pretty involved with the community... planning meetings, helping out with events. But lately, I've just... pulled back. I don't really go anymore. I just feel so drained, and... embarrassed, I guess. I worry people are going to see that I'm not... that I don't have it all together like I used to. So I just stay home.
